gates.name: The pull request is tied to a refined issue, and a data-model change has an ADR for that story
gates.checks: It finds the story key in the branch, title, body or closing issues, and checks with `gh` that the issue has the refined label. A data-model change needs an ADR for the story that the pull request adds or changes. An older ADR of the same story does not count, but a `No-ADR` commit trailer with a why does. Exit 2 means `gh` or its token is missing, and exit 3 means there is no pull request context.
gates.fix: Name a refined issue in the branch, the title or the body, and add an ADR for a data-model change, or a `No-ADR` trailer.

gates.name: Each issue that an ADR names points back at that ADR
gates.checks: It reads an ADR only when the change adds or changes its `story:` line. It reads the issue body with `gh`, and warns when the body does not mention the ADR. Exit 2 means no issue body could be read or there is no merge base. Exit 3 means no ADR story line changed or the run is not GitHub Actions.
gates.fix: Add the ADR to the Decisions and ADRs section of the issue body, and quote the story key in the ADR front matter.
